- at least 4 modules

Planning - Step 1

Ideas

final module - add modules of each option and print results

## Introduction

The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) and California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) is considering the replacement of the Sandia Creek Drive crossing with a new bridge by 2027 will reconnect over twelve miles of habitat along the Santa Margarita River for endangered Southern California Steelhead trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss irideus) in northern San Diego County. The Santa Margarita river would be the first perennially-flowing river in Southern California with no anadromous fish migration barriers in its mainstem. The new bridge would also improve emergency response access and evacuation reliability, as its proposed design can withstand a 100-year storm event without overtopping with flowing water.

The agencies wish to compare costs of two options: no action (keeping the existing bridge) and constructing a new bridge. The option with the lowest cost will be chosen moving forward.

The following program uses several modules to compare cost scenarios:

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("flowchart.jpg")
```

The following R packages are needed for this program:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

```{r}
# set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(262)

# Generate 365 steps: changes are either -1, 0, or 1
changes <- sample(c(-1, 0, 1), 365, replace = TRUE)
river_ht <- 8 + cumsum(changes) # Optimal river height is 8 meters, flooding when height > 20m

  day = seq(1,365),
  river_ht
)
```

### Option 2: Construct New Bridge

#### 2.1 Calculate the cost of Materials

Inputs: river height data

Outputs: total material costs in \$ for flood delays

```{r}
# Module 2.1

material_cost <- function(river_height_data,
                          base_material_cost = 2000000,
                          flood_threshold = 20,
                          cost_per_day = 10000) {

  delay_days <- 0  # count construction delay days due to flooding

  for (i in 1:nrow(river_height_data)) {
    if (river_height_data$river_ht[i] > flood_threshold) {
      delay_days <- delay_days + 1
    }
  }

  total_material <- base_material_cost + (delay_days * delay_cost_per_day)

  return(total_material)
}
```

#### 2.2 Calculate the cost of Labor

Input: river height data

Output: total labor cost in dollars accounting for flood

```{r}
# Module 2.2

labor_cost <- function(river_height_data,
                       workers = 40,
                       daily_wage = 350,
                       flood_threshold = 20,
                       work_days = 365) {

  days_worked <- 0  # only count non-flood days as billable

  for (i in 1:nrow(river_height_data)) {
    if (river_height_data$river_ht[i] <= flood_threshold) {
      days_worked <- days_worked + 1
    }
  }

  # Workers are still paid on flood days (they can't work but are on contract)
  total_labor <- workers * daily_wage * work_days

  return(total_labor)
}
```

workers - number of workers on site (\~40)

daily_wage - daily wage per worker in dollars (\~\$350)

flood_threshold - river height that halts work (\~20m)

work_days - total planned construction workdays (\~365)

#### Total Cost of Option 2

### Compare Option 1 vs Option 2

```{r}
# Module 3 - compare_costs()
#   Input:  op1 & op2
#   Output: cost comparison

compare_costs <- function(op1, op2) {

  op1_fmt <- format(round(op1), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
  op2_fmt <- format(round(op2), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
  diff    <- format(round(abs(op1 - op2)), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)

  cat("=== Bridge Cost Comparison ===\n")
  cat(sprintf("Option 1 (No Action):    $%s\n", op1_fmt))
  cat(sprintf("Option 2 (New Bridge):   $%s\n", op2_fmt))
  cat("------------------------------\n")

  if (op1 < op2) {
    cat(sprintf("Recommendation: Keep existing bridge. Saves $%s.\n", diff))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("Recommendation: Build new bridge. Saves $%s over time.\n", diff))
  }
}

```
